All six GEOIDs have a provided MTBS last-wildfire year of 2018. The table compares challenge summaries with incident-filtered public CAL FIRE Camp Fire DINS inspection points. The CAL FIRE feature-service layer was retrieved 2026-10-29; its catalogue records CC BY (version unspecified), and the layer does not provide a more specific licence statement. Only incident, damage class, county, object ID, and point geometry were requested; raw data and manifest remain outside git.

Ratio is Overture / `usfs_BuildingCount_sum`; relative error is `abs((USFS − Overture) − DINS destroyed) / DINS destroyed`. Values are in `reports/discovery-postfire.json#/focal_butte_2018_burn_geoids` and `reports/discovery-dins-mechanism.json#/focal_butte_tracts`; the workspace manifest pins the raw file.
Burn classes follow the report's 0–100% bins; tracts reported above 100% are omitted rather than clipped (`reports/discovery-postfire.json#/burn_definition`).
These provided-data class counts and proportions are at `reports/discovery-postfire.json#/northern_ca_burn_class_table`. The one map shows the burn geography and the six focal tracts:
![NorCal/Butte tract map: fill is provided MTBS burned percentage; the six focal tracts are marked.](../../reports/discovery-postfire-map.png)

The tract-bootstrap difference is +9.55 percentage points (95% CI [+0.55, +20.89]; 50,000 replicates; valid-replicate fraction 1.0). The county-cluster bootstrap 95% interval [-1.65, +16.67] includes zero, so the magnitude remains exploratory (`reports/discovery-postfire-county-bootstrap.json#/county_cluster_bootstrap/cluster_95_percentile_interval`).

**DINS mechanism reproduction check — negative.** The DINS reproduction check did **not** confirm the proposed fire-damage/rebuilding mechanism: 0/6 focal tracts met the relative-error threshold (tolerance) of ≤0.30 (the rule required at least 4/6), and Spearman was 0.4626068 across all 28 last-burn-2018 tracts, below the 0.60 threshold (`reports/discovery-dins-mechanism.json#/decision`, `#/spearman`). DINS therefore does not substantiate the hypothesised mechanism. Across 591 NorCal tracts, 576 have positive Overture counts but no Camp Fire DINS record, totaling 1,139,778 buildings; because this is an inspection-limited, incident-specific source, a missing record cannot establish absence or rebuilding (`reports/discovery-dins-mechanism.json#/opposite_direction`). Focal MTBS percentages are cumulative (64.4–153.8%), and the count field's exact vintage is unverified. DINS is discovery-only; no removed reference was accessed. No external public data was used outside this DINS check; source-mix and strata checks use provided data only.

In the official sample, 805 of 858 tracts marked `tribal_any` (93.82%, approximately 94%) are in Eastern Oklahoma, while 6,002 of 8,521 non-tribal tracts (70.44%, approximately 70%) are in South-Central Texas (`reports/discovery-strata-confound.json#/stratum_composition`). The breakdown is reproducible from `reports/discovery-strata-confound.json#/regional_counts_and_prevalence`.

The deterministic C2/v0 screen uses only provided Overture feature summaries and allowed provided covariates (`ALAND`, `pop_total`, `pop_urban`, `pct_urban`). Geometry from the supplied ACS housing tract files is used solely for spatial clipping/tract assignment; no ACS housing count is read. Road geometry is clipped to authoritative sample tract polygons and measured in EPSG:5070; building/POI bbox centers are assigned to tracts. Exact formulas and audit lineage are in `reports/gap-estimator-audit.json`.

| Component | C2/v0 expected reference proxy | Definedness and component calculation |
|---|---|---|
| Transport | `0.35 + 0.55*sqrt(ALAND_km2) + 0.0007*pop_total + 2*urban_fraction` (expected named-road km) | Defined when expectation ≥6 km. Gap=`clip(1−overture_named_road_km/expected,0,1)`. |
| Buildings | `max(0.5,0.30*pop_total + 4*sqrt(ALAND_km2) + 5*urban_fraction)` (expected structures) | Defined when observed Overture buildings >0 or expectation ≥1. Gap=`clip(1−observed/expected,0,1)`. ACS housing units are not a floor or denominator. |
| Fire / EMS / schools | Fire=`0.15+pop/30000+0.45*u`; EMS=`0.15+pop/40000+0.45*u`; schools=`0.20+pop/2500+0.20*u` | Each type defined when observed count >0 or expected count ≥0.5. Gap per defined type is clipped `1−observed/expected`; facility half averages only defined types. |
| Establishments half | `0.20 + pop/70 + 0.50*u` (v0 proxy) | Defined when all-place Overture count >0 or expected establishments ≥1. Gap=`clip(1−observed/expected,0,1)`. No CBP data is accessed. |
| POI | Mean of defined facility half and establishments half | Equal-weight defined halves; if only one is defined, use that half; if neither is defined, POI is undefined. |
| Tract composite | No new denominator | Equal mean of defined transport, building, and POI components; undefined terms are omitted. If none are defined, no composite is emitted. |

For missing urbanity, use finite `pct_urban`; otherwise use `pop_urban/pop_total` when population is positive; if both are unavailable at zero population, use the disclosed neutral 0.5 fallback. In the proxy expected-reference formulas, land area is floored at 0.01 km². Unknown-category POIs are apportioned using the in-sample selected-category share in the legacy v0 screen, not treated as category-specific zeroes. These heuristics are explicit assumptions, not learned parameters. A serialized zero attached to `defined=0` is only a storage placeholder and is excluded from all means.

The audit finds 26 zero-population tracts, 2 zero-`ALAND` tracts, 43 tracts with a >50% water proxy, 132 with no selected named roads, 2,644 with no selected route-network km, 2 with no Overture buildings, 2 with no Overture places, and 26 missing `pct_urban` values. These are covariate/coverage characteristics, not hidden-score outcomes. The audit also reports fixed-prior v2 component distributions for zero-population, water-proxy, and other edge groups. The expected facility gap is `P(reference present) × conditional gap`, so low prior presence yields proportionally small expected gaps; missing `pct_urban` falls back to `pop_urban/pop_total`, or neutral 0.5 at zero population. These are component diagnostics; the establishments half is not part of the submitted score. The water statistic is only `max(0,min(1,1−ALAND/geometry_area))` after projecting provided tract geometry to EPSG:5070; it is not an external water mask or a scoring correction.

claims.text: The opt-in route audit is `scripts/estimate_gaps.py --route-audit-only`. It reads only the provided Overture roads `class`, `routes`, and `geometry` columns, official sample GEOIDs, the provided ACS tract `GEOID`/`geometry` solely for clipping, and the existing v0 component flags for an any-undefined comparison. It reads no TIGER or other road reference data, labels, sample score placeholders, or leaderboard values. Named classes remain `motorway`, `trunk`, `primary`, and `secondary`; the v0 `overture_road_km` field is preserved. The v2 `L_named` is independently clipped in EPSG:5070 as `overture_named_road_km_5070`; the v2 `L_route` is the length of each segment once if it carries at least one accepted route network, also clipped in EPSG:5070. The score term is `clip(1 - L_named/L_route, 0, 1)`, defined only for `L_route > 0` (undefined rows serialize gap 0 with `defined=0`).

The route filter accepts interstate (`US:I*`), U.S. (`US:US*`), state-level (`US:<state>` plus explicit SR, loop, spur, beltway, future, alternate, and bypass variants), and county `US:<state>:CR*` networks. It rejects historic/business and scenic networks (`NHT`, `NFSR`/`NFRS`, scenic tokens), missing network values, and unsupported non-route systems. County-name namespaces such as `US:OK:ADAIR` are listed but not treated as numbered county routes without an explicit `:CR` class. A segment with multiple accepted route networks contributes once to `L_route`; per-family length columns can overlap. `overture_route_core_km` and `overture_route_plus_fm_rm_km` are cached separately so the declared Texas FM/RM sensitivity can be measured without re-reading/reclassifying target data. Since the existing repository already used aggregate cache schema v5 for source-mix features, route caches use aggregate schema v6 (base) or v7 (with source mix) and `route_schema_version=1`.

All four route-v2 transport + v0 building/POI any-undefined shares are within 0.10 of the disclosed region shares; they are a hybrid check, not a full v2 composite. Three of four length ratios meet the lane's broad 0.6–1.7 check; Maricopa is 1.929 and remains out of band even with all accepted state, U.S., Interstate, loop, and explicit county-route networks. The report identifies this as a denominator-coverage failure rather than adding prohibited scenic/business, missing-network, or unclassified county-name routes to force a ratio. In Northern California the observed route-entry counts reproduce `US:CA` 6,055, `US:CA:CR` 2,190, `US:US` 1,024, and `US:I` 861; the report lists all kept/dropped networks and counts for each region, per-tract `L_route` quantiles/bins, and v0 comparisons. The disclosed ratio band (0.71–1.59) and undefined shares are aggregate validation context only, not calibration targets. This is a route mechanism audit, not a validated accuracy result or assembled candidate.

hedge_context: `scripts/build_road_topology_candidate.py` preregisters `ROAD_TOPOLOGY_ROUTE_REF_V1` in `config/road-topology-preregistered.json`. It uses only the provided Overture road `class`, `connectors`, and `geometry` columns, official sample GEOIDs, provided ACS tract geometry for assignment, `pct_urban` strata, and the provided route-length cache. For each provided segment, connector points are interpolated from the connector's normalized `at` position; successive connector IDs form adjacency edges. The tract-local graph contains unique connector IDs assigned to that official tract and a simple undirected edge only when both endpoints of a successive connector pair map to the same tract. Cross-tract edges are counted but not included in the local graph; duplicate unordered edges are collapsed for degree/components. Isolated connector vertices are retained. Thus the reported graph is a tract-induced structural summary, not a routing/access network or independent truth source. The hypothesis is motivated by the road-completeness prior art in [`docs/literature/completeness-prior-art.md`](../literature/completeness-prior-art.md) and Overture's connector schema, but no global OSM rate or external road evidence is transferred into the candidate.

It reconciles exactly to the frozen route-reference audit for each region's named/route length sums, route-zero count, and defined-only mean. Across 9,379 tracts the route-reference candidate is defined for 6,735 (71.81%), with a defined-only mean of `0.03166`; its numeric all-row mean (undefined rows stored as zero with a flag) is `0.02273`. The prior v0 transport component is defined for 5,914 (63.06%) and has all-row mean `0.09683`. The measure-before report also records legacy/named/route length distributions overall, by region, and by rural/urban `pct_urban` strata.

The frozen adjustment is `0.05 × (1 − largest_component_node_share)` and is added to the route-reference gap only on route-defined rows; route-undefined rows retain numeric zero and `defined=0`. This is a positive bounded context sensitivity, not a fit to a reference. Topology diagnostics were available for 9,377/9,379 tracts (99.98%). Across tracts, local components have median 6 and p95 34; mean dead-end-node share is 14.54%, mean degree is 2.24, median largest-component node share is 93.68%, and isolated single-node components average 3.40 per tract. The candidate adjustment mean/median/p95/max over all rows is `0.00513/0.00149/0.02409/0.04358`; 67.45% of rows change. Among route-defined rows, the route-reference gap mean changes from `0.03166` to `0.03880`. Regional candidate delta means range from `0.00321` (Maricopa) to `0.00571` (South-Central Texas); the full region × rural/urban degree, component, adjustment, definedness, and road-length tables are in `reports/road-topology-candidate.json`.

The edge audit processed 3,143,887 supplied road-segment rows and 8,491,546 connector occurrences. It skipped 1,087 segments with invalid/non-LineString geometry after valid connector parsing, observed 1,591 connector points outside the official tract polygons, and excluded 245,818 within-package adjacencies whose endpoints fell in different tracts. Two South-Central Texas tracts had no assigned connector nodes. These boundary/geometry cases are disclosed in the report and do not cause an unbounded fallback. The per-tract candidate is finite and in `[0,1]`; maximum actual change is `0.04358`, below the fixed `0.05` limit. Two complete builds were byte-identical. Candidate CSV SHA-256 is `612c2080c3d470fbcdc0cd752cd26847da05a35bf5d245c0b1599134cc82fda7`; manifest SHA-256 is `b269e4487905937d48418822aeb11a92e76f0371236d99e175e920d82852705f`.

Connector degrees/components can reflect cul-de-sacs, ramps, package edges, or schema/source artifacts and do not establish missing real-world roads or predictive accuracy. No local target RMSE is possible or claimed. Reproduce with:
